title: Understanding k-Means Clustering
text: In k-Means clustering, each point is assigned to the cluster whose center is closest to it. The center of a cluster is the average of all the points assigned to it. Think about how you can calculate the average of the coordinates for each cluster.

title: Calculating Distance
text: To determine which cluster a point belongs to, calculate the distance from the point to each cluster center. Use the formula for Euclidean distance: distance between (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) is $$\sqrt{\left(x2-x1\right)^2+\left(y2-y1\right)^2}$$.

title: Assigning Teams to Clusters
text: Which team is closest to the initial center of cluster A at $$(0,5)$$?

hintAnswer: Calculate the average of the coordinates of the points in the cluster.
title: Recalculating Cluster Centers
text: After assigning teams to clusters, how do you find the new center of a cluster?
choices: >Calculate the average of the coordinates of the points in the cluster
>Use the midpoint of the farthest points in the cluster
Calculate the average of the coordinates of the points in the cluster.
Choose the point closest to the current center

title: Convergence in k-Means
text: The algorithm converges when the cluster centers no longer change after an iteration. This means the assignments of points to clusters remain the same.
